question: Why does unchanged original grain-shirt develop high material-axis strain during zero-gravity sewing, and does the current 3ed source mesh change the historical result?

baseline.name: current_control_8x32
baseline.supported_contact: production core bridge, all original mannequin, ground, self and interpanel contacts enabled

independent_observables: Original UV/triangle area masses independently reconstructed and compared to public solver masses; rest versus arranged strain with piece grain angles
Every-frame signed warp/weft length strains and locations, maximum extension and compression, membrane energies from documented Green strain energy
Bending energies from original rest adjacency/dihedrals; conservative bending forces at predeclared frames 0,30,45,60,180 via local central differences epsilon 1e-6 m
Conservative membrane and sewing energy gradients/forces from UV and source seam mapping, not implementation diagnostics; membrane force analytic derivative self-checked by central differences
Sampled stitch gaps and assembly target from original initial gap minus declared actuator travel; independent capsule/ground penetration (not independent full self-contact proof)

Total mass, center of mass, kinetic energy, linear and angular momentum from original positions/masses and velocities; every-frame delta momentum/dt and nodal m*delta_velocity/dt are interval effective net force, not instantaneous force equilibrium

Authored seam side lengths, original correspondence orientation, arranged weighted-point gaps/offsets and conditional body/neck/cuff circumference bounds from source seam graph; report direction-dependent/shear limitations of axis strain
Current versus historical mesh positions, UV, triangles, piece IDs, stitches, masses; same-time positional differences only where node identity agrees; historical states never relabeled current
Final and assembly quality outcomes with original failed thresholds visible

hypotheses_and_discriminators.discriminator: Independent rest F and rest energy distinguish prestrain from sewing-induced strain

hypotheses_and_discriminators.hypothesis: Seam orientation or unequal source edge lengths force a mismatch
hypotheses_and_discriminators.discriminator: Independent seam interval endpoints/lengths and sampled source correspondence; equal sides and common arranged x/y reject this simple explanation but do not prove global fitting
Temporary targets and actual weighted gaps below fixed seam screen distinguish unclosed assembly from cloth strain after closure

hypotheses_and_discriminators.hypothesis: Current mesh scheduling changes the result
hypotheses_and_discriminators.discriminator: Exact current versus e342 mesh arrays/masses and full-path endpoint comparison; no numerical values presumed current before this run

hypotheses_and_discriminators.hypothesis: Geometric fit or avatar reaction drives local high strain without gravity
hypotheses_and_discriminators.discriminator: Locate high strain with source seam/neck/cuff geometry and collider clearance; conditional circumference bounds cannot alone establish 15% axis-strain impossibility

hypotheses_and_discriminators.hypothesis: Residual assembly dynamics or finite solver convergence produces strain
hypotheses_and_discriminators.discriminator: Energy, momentum and nodal effective-force changes quantify continued motion; at most two later preregistered targeted probes may distinguish zero-G relaxation, contact loading or substep sensitivity; no equilibrium or defect inference from low speed

sequence_and_budget.first: Run exactly one fixed original current-source baseline before selecting a probe
sequence_and_budget.later_cases: Only with a concrete unresolved question and append-only preregistration after baseline analysis. Preserve all original inputs and failures. No broad sweep, no blind time extension, no material/default/fixture/tolerance tuning.
